chunks: Or is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them, theirs? Then let them climb up the ladders (to the heavens).

key_terms.الْأَسْبَابِ: The ladders, paths, or means (of ascent)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'climb up the ladders' mean in Surah Sad?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to polytheists and those claiming divine authority, questioning their ability to ascend the 'ladders' (al-asbab) to the heavens if they truly possess cosmic dominion. It underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah, contrasting human limitation with divine power, and is often linked to the concept of Tawhid (monotheism) in contrast to the claims of various sects. The 'ladders' are interpreted variously as paths of ascent or means of connection, highlighting the futility of those who assert exclusive control over the universe.
